Where it began

Aiden Markram was born in Centurion on 4 October 1994. He spent a short time at Cornwall Hill College before moving to Pretoria Boys High School, chosen for its strong sporting tradition and facilities, and the move paid off.

He was a leader early. In 2014 he captained South Africa to the Under-19 World Cup title, and later that year he made his first-class debut for Northerns. In 2016 he spent an English summer as the club professional at Walkden in the Bolton League, and a year after that he was named South Africa's domestic newcomer of the year.

The player

His Test debut came against Bangladesh in September 2017. He fell just short of a hundred in that first match, then made 143 in the second, and by December he was the first South African with a hundred in two of his first three Tests. In March 2018 he made 152 against Australia, his highest Test score.

By November 2026 he had played 53 Tests, scoring 3,394 runs at 35.73 with eight hundreds, and he had held 77 catches. His finest Test came in 2025. In the World Test Championship final against Australia he made 136 in the second innings, South Africa won by five wickets, and he was named player of the match.

What made him special

He was marked out as a leader from the start, and Graeme Smith spoke of him early on as a future South Africa captain. He has captained his country in all three formats, and in Tests he led South Africa to three wins in four matches. In 2024 he became the first South African captain to take a side to a men's T20 World Cup final.

Spin bowling on tours of Asia took him a little longer to work out, and his early Tests in Asia were lean ones. He worked through it. In Pakistan in 2021 he made his first hundred in Asia and finished as the leading run-scorer of the series.

Away from the middle

He has been a thoughtful captain in franchise cricket too, leading Sunrisers Eastern Cape to the first two SA20 titles and later captaining Sunrisers Hyderabad in the Indian Premier League. He has also played county cricket for Hampshire. The South African Cricket Annual named him one of its five Cricketers of the Year in 2018.

He can change gear when he likes. At the 2023 World Cup he reached a hundred against Sri Lanka in 49 balls, at the time the fastest in the history of the men's tournament.

And finally

In a Test against India in November 2025 he held nine catches, more than anyone had managed in a single Test before. India's batters that week may have felt that edging the ball anywhere near him was much the same as walking off.
